tob-10022: Vincent Scully’s short biography profiles a medieval mystic, recounting the main events of his life and the heart of what he taught. Mystics were religious seekers who claimed to experience God directly, and the Middle Ages produced many of them. This little book gives modern readers a clear window into one such life and the spiritual path he followed.
tob-10222: Sigmund Freud’s landmark 1900 work argues that dreams are not random but coded messages from the unconscious mind. Analyzing his own dreams and those of his patients, he shows how dreams disguise forbidden wishes through symbols that can be decoded. This is A. A. Brill’s English translation. The book launched psychoanalysis and changed how the twentieth century understood the mind.
tob-10622: Shinran, the thirteenth-century founder of Japan’s Pure Land Buddhism, taught that salvation comes not through one’s own effort but through trust in the boundless compassion of Amida Buddha. These psalms and hymns express that simple, radical faith in verse. L. Adams Beck’s translation brings the devotional heart of Japanese Buddhism to English readers.
tob-10822: Reynold Nicholson, the great English scholar of Sufism, introduces the mystics of Islam in this compact classic. He explains the Sufi path — its love poetry, its ecstatic practices, its great figures like Rumi and al-Hallaj — with a scholar’s precision and a poet’s sympathy. The book remains one of the finest short guides to Islamic mysticism.
tob-4022: Bishop Berkeley argues, in a witty back-and-forth, that the stuff of the world exists only as seen — ‘to be is to be perceived.’ Hylas stands up for common sense; Philonous gently takes it apart. The result is one of thought’s most graceful and unnerving books, a dare aimed at all we think we know.
tob-0122: Samuel Rowbotham, as ‘Parallax,’ pleads the flat-earth case with measures, trials, and homespun reckoning. He held that the Bedford Level tests proved the earth a plain, and built a whole heaven-and-earth to fit. The book sired the latter-day flat-earth drive, which runs on still.
tob-4222: Thorold’s Englishing of St. Catherine’s Talk gives her converse with God — on heaven’s foreseeing, lowly worship, and the church’s mending. Breathed forth in rapture, it ranks with the great holy classics. Her fiery Italian now speaks our tongue. The book bares a saint shaping story.
tob-13322: St. John of the Cross’s Dark Night — in Lewis’s Englishing — is the great barefoot-friar’s tract on the soul’s sore cleansing. The Spanish holy man charts the dark road to God-oneness. His song and prose rank with the finest Christian inwardness. The work stays the classic guide to the dark night.
cia-0000109822: A September 1945 file on Frederick Wiehl, alias Captain Awald — a man with two names in the ruins of postwar Europe. False identities were the currency of fugitives, spies, and war criminals alike. The entry is a single card in the vast Allied effort to sort the guilty from the merely displaced.
cia-0000112822: A January 1945 file on name checks against Colonel Fox-Holmes's files. In wartime intelligence, verifying a name against a trusted officer's records could mean the difference between an ally and a plant. The entry is a sliver of the unglamorous verification work behind every operation.
cia-0000117922: A February 1955 item on the Alsop brothers joining the preachers of atomic war — Joseph and Stewart Alsop were America's most influential columnists. arxiv-2605-09022: Smashing protons together sprays hadrons — pions, kaons, protons — and counting each species tests our theories. Rishabh Gupta, Kangkan Goswami, Suraj Prasad, and colleagues infer identified hadron production in proton-proton collisions with physics-informed machine learning. The 2026 paper is particle physics with AI that respects the laws.
arxiv-2605-09222: Server logs hide anomalies that precede outages, and operators need more than red flags. Lei Ma, Suhani Chaudhary, Ethan Shanbaum, and colleagues build interactive hierarchical log anomaly analytics with LLM augmentation — detect, localize, and explain. The 2026 paper is AIOps that tells you why, not just what.
arxiv-2605-09122: Topological quantum codes protect information in the fabric of spacetime itself, and heat threatens them. Nafiz Ishtiaque and Shanto Chakroborty construct an exact spacetime polymer gas for finite-temperature Z_N homological quantum codes. The 2026 paper is quantum error correction with statistical-physics muscle.
arxiv-2605-09522: Emotions between embodied agents might emerge from communication itself — co-constructed through interaction rather than programmed in. Zehang Zhang, Nguyen Le Hoang, Tadahiro Taniguchi, and colleagues explore this emergence via collective predictive coding. The 2026 paper is where artificial life meets affective science.
arxiv-2605-09822: Poison the knowledge graph and the agent reasons with lies. Ben Kereopa-Yorke, Guillermo Diaz, Holly Wright, and colleagues demonstrate oracle poisoning: corrupting knowledge graphs to weaponise AI agent reasoning. The 2026 paper is AI security at the source of truth.
arxiv-2605-09922: Self-play fine-tunes LLMs against themselves; team-based play with dual adaptive weighting sharpens the contest. Yigeng Zhou, Zesheng Shi, Yequan Wang, and colleagues develop the team-based method. The 2026 paper is LLM training reimagined as a truly competitive team sport today.
arxiv-2605-10022: The Bullet Cluster — two galaxy clusters mid-collision — still shows residual missing mass beyond what the visible matter explains. Benoit Famaey examines that leftover mystery. The 2026 paper is dark matter astrophysics on the most famous collision in the sky. It hunts the missing mass.
plos-pone-0003422: Blood-cell researchers found a disposal tag controlling white blood cells in this 2008 paper. The G-CSF receptor drives the birth of infection-fighting granulocytes, and the team showed that tagging it with ubiquitin, the cell's demolition label, critically regulates the cells' survival and growth. Faulty tagging helps explain severe congenital neutropenia, where patients cannot make enough of these defenders.
plos-pone-0003522: Cognitive neuroscientists reverse-engineered willpower in this 2008 paper. The brain constantly chooses which information deserves attention, and the team probed the algorithms behind that voluntary control. Their experiments reveal the computational rules the mind uses to marshal its limited resources toward what matters most.
plos-pone-0003622: Neuroscientists Aleman and Swart found men and women reading scorn differently in this 2008 brain study. Contempt, the emotion of moral superiority, and its cousin disgust lit up distinct activation patterns by sex when volunteers viewed facial expressions. The gendered neural signatures show social emotions are processed through different neural lenses.
plos-pone-0003722: In 2008, Ferrante, Anderson, and Klug caught an immune editor comparison-shopping. HLA-DM helps choose which protein fragments get shown to the immune system, and the team showed it works by a compare-and-exchange routine when many candidate peptides are around. The mechanism reveals quality control in immune display.
plos-pone-0003822: Back in 2008, a group engineered a Swiss-army tag for protein research. Their new multifunctional green fluorescent protein label works for live imaging, purification, and more in one package. The versatile tag gives labs a single tool for many protein-tracking jobs.
plos-pone-0003922: In 2008, Moioli, Clark, and Chen paired two stem cell types to grow blood vessels. Blood-forming and mesenchymal progenitors together vascularized engineered tissue better than either alone. The synergy tackles the top roadblock in tissue repair: getting vessels to grow in. The paired-cell approach brings lab-grown replacement tissues closer to working.
plos-pone-0004022: In 2008, Green, Hunt, and Parish tested whether condors were dodging lead. Actions to cut lead exposure in free-ranging California condors were carefully evaluated. Blood lead levels in the Arizona and Utah birds tracked the interventions. The effectiveness study guides the ongoing fight to keep condors lead-free.
plos-pone-0004122: In 2009, a team turned flu into an immune alarm. A weakened influenza A vaccine virus sparked immediate killer activity in blood immune cells. The delNS1 virus woke all major mononuclear subsets at once. The loud alarm explains the vaccine's punch.
plos-pone-0004222: In 2009, Johnston, Orem, and Okuku tracked a cancer virus in Uganda. HIV infection and Kaposi sarcoma boosted human herpesvirus-8 mucosal replication. The virus shed more in affected patients. The shedding data guide transmission control. The work clarifies how co-infection fuels viral spread.
plos-pone-0004322: In 2009, Nunes and Silva searched blood for hidden heart clues. Systemic markers were correlated with angiographic coronary artery disease. The blood signals tracked artery narrowing. The correlations may yield simple risk tests soon. The work points toward cheaper heart screening.
plos-pone-0357022: HIV programs in Ethiopia run on health data — but only if the data is good. This study evaluated the quality and actual use of Health Management Information System data for HIV/AIDS programs in Jimma town’s public facilities. The audit shows where the numbers break down and how to fix them.
plos-pone-0358422: Back surgery is riskier with diabetes — but how much? This large-scale study linked type 2 diabetes to postoperative outcomes after single-level endoscopic lumbar interbody fusion. The results quantify the added risk, helping surgeons and diabetic patients weigh the decision.
plos-pone-0352922: Capelin are the ocean’s forage fish — but do they stay home or roam? Using otolith (ear-stone) chemistry, this paper weighed regional fidelity against dispersal of capelin in the Gulf of St. Lawrence. The chemical fingerprints reveal which fish are locals and which are travelers passing through.
plos-pone-0358122: Who falls in love with anesthesiology during medical school — and when? This study linked demographic characteristics to the evolution of interest in the specialty across the medical school years. The patterns help recruiters understand who chooses this behind-the-scenes field and what draws them in.
plos-pone-0357622: Ultrasound can watch tendons heal in real time after rotator cuff repair. This systematic review examined the application of musculoskeletal ultrasound in postoperative rehabilitation assessment and monitoring. The synthesized evidence shows exactly what the probe reveals — and when clinicians should look.
plos-pone-0357922: Noninvasive heartbeat sensors — from optical to radar — vary wildly in what they capture. This paper characterized the time and frequency characteristics of various sensor types. The head-to-head comparison guides engineers and clinicians toward the right device for each job.
plos-pone-0350622: Variants in the MDM2 gene — a master regulator of the p53 tumor suppressor — may raise breast cancer risk. This case-control study linked MDM2 polymorphisms to cancer susceptibility and circulating MDM2 and p53 levels in Bangladeshi women. The genetics could one day inform targeted screening.
plos-pone-0356722: Urinary cell-free DNA — a promising liquid biopsy — lives or dies by how the sample is handled. This paper studied the impact of preanalytical variables on its quality: centrifugation, EDTA concentration, storage, and thawing strategies. The findings standardize handling so results can be trusted.
plos-pone-0356822: Interpreting uterine cultures in mares has long been more art than science. This paper brought evidence to bear, linking bacterial growth patterns to endometrial inflammation. The findings give equine veterinarians a rational framework for deciding which positive cultures truly mean infection — and which to ignore.
plos-pone-0354822: Even vaccinated adults can suffer severe COVID-19 — but which ones? This retrospective Alberta cohort study examined factors associated with severe outcomes among adults with at least primary vaccination. The findings refine risk stratification in the vaccine era — guiding boosters and treatments to those who still need them most.
plos-pone-0351822: Seagrass meadows — ocean nurseries — need restoration at scale. This paper refined the use of seed balls to support seagrass restoration. The improved technique promises cheaper, more reliable meadow recovery — a win for coastlines, carbon storage, and marine life alike.
plos-pone-0355722: Nurses and physiotherapists must learn together — but barriers abound. This scoping review mapped the facilitators and barriers to interprofessional learning between the two professions in hospital practice. The synthesis gives educators the evidence to build training that genuinely bridges professional divides.
plos-pone-0345722: Spotting tiny targets in infrared imagery — drones, missiles, people — is brutally hard. RSFNet — a retention-based network with spatial–frequency joint enhancement — tackles infrared small target detection. The dual-domain enhancement finds the faint heat signatures that conventional detectors miss.
europmc-pmc2820522: Lupus strikes Asian populations hard, yet most genetic studies had focused on Europeans. This 2010 genome-wide association study in Asian populations finds variants in the ETS1 and WDFY4 genes linked to systemic lupus erythematosus. The discovery filled a diversity gap in lupus genetics. It pointed to immune pathways that could guide new treatments.
europmc-pmc2935122: What the world eats is shifting fast. This 2010 paper reviews food consumption trends and what drives them, from income to cities. The author maps the forces reshaping diets. Their overview informs food policy for a hungry planet. Meat, sugar, and processed foods all rise.
europmc-pmc2976722: Clean water and toilets save more lives than high-tech medicine. This 2010 paper calls hygiene, sanitation, and water the forgotten foundations of health. The authors' plea recenters basics. Their paper influenced global health priorities. Donors shifted funds toward taps and latrines.
europmc-pmc3101722: Cancer imaging got a PET/CT guide. This 2011 paper reviews sugar-tracer PET/CT scans for finding tumors. The authors survey the technique. Their overview guides radiologists. Hungry tumors glow on the scans. The guide standardizes scan reading. Staging got sharper with PET/CT.
europmc-pmc6538222: The Keap1-Nrf2-ARE pathway is the cell's smoke detector: Keap1 senses oxidative danger and releases Nrf2, which switches on hundreds of protective genes. This review details how the pathway damps inflammation and oxidative damage in chronic diseases from diabetes to arthritis. Because the system is druggable, it is a prized target for medicines that boost the body's own defenses.
europmc-pmc6560022: Canagliflozin - a diabetes drug that flushes sugar through urine - also slows kidney decline, and scientists hunted for why. Tracking blood markers, they found the drug lowers signs of inflammation and scarring in the kidneys. The result hints that taming inflammation and fibrosis is part of how this drug class protects organs beyond blood sugar.
europmc-pmc6637122: Cigarette smoke may rot lungs from within by triggering ferroptosis - iron-driven cell suicide - in airway lining cells. This study links smoke-induced ferroptosis to COPD's destructive course. The mechanism offers a fresh explanation for smoker's lung decline and a new target for slowing it.
europmc-pmc6715822: Malaria's best drugs are failing in the Mekong - parasites shrug off artemisinin combinations. This trial dissected why dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine fails in Cambodia: the genetic markers and blood levels behind treatment failure. The findings are a fire alarm for global malaria control.
europmc-pmc6769522: Heart disease simmers in oxidative stress - but can antioxidants douse it? This review asks whether oxidative stress remains a therapeutic target in cardiovascular disease, weighing decades of mixed trial results. The verdict is cautious: the biology is real, the drugs not yet.
europmc-pmc6770822: Olive oil, vegetables, fish - the Mediterranean diet keeps topping healthy-eating charts. This review examines its link to cancer: the antioxidant and anti-inflammatory foods that may lower risk. The pattern is consistent - the sun-drenched plate protects.
europmc-pmc6776522: Killing staph with heat works - but the heat harms healthy tissue too. This study built zinc-doped Prussian blue nanoparticles that cook Staphylococcus aureus with light while sparing surroundings, then help tissue regrow. The targeted heaters turn photothermal therapy antibacterial.
europmc-pmc6777022: Prediction models are only useful if they change decisions - decision curve analysis tests exactly that. This step-by-step guide teaches clinicians to read and interpret decision curves without the mystique. The plain-language tour turns a confusing method into a practical tool.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-122: This 2007 GAO report tells the Pentagon to show its math on the new medical chain of command. The report is a demand for homework before the brass rearranges the military's doctors.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-622: Underground miners needed a better safety net in 2007 — GAO's report says the mine agency and its partners could tighten watch and teamwork. The findings target the oversight gaps below ground. The report's demand: no miner should die for a paperwork failure.
gao-gaoreports-b-308822: A building mishap ate the Archives' books in this 2007 GAO ruling — damage to the revolving fund's records from a facility failure. The call sorts the fiscal fallout. Even the keepers of history, the ruling shows, can lose their own paperwork.
gao-gaoreports-b-299422: Information Ventures doubled its May 2007 protest — two case numbers, one information-services fight — and GAO's combined ruling settles both claims at once. gao-gaoreports-gao-07-522: The privacy office was learning to speak up in 2007 — GAO's report says notifying the public had improved, but hard challenges stayed. The findings grade the outreach effort honestly. The report's standard: the watched deserve to know that they are being watched.
gao-gaoreports-b-299022: Wackenhut's joint venture doubled its January 2007 protest — two case numbers, one security fight — and GAO's combined ruling settles both. gao-gaoreports-gao-07-22: The pension cops were improving in 2007, and GAO's report says enforcement had gotten better, though more action could help. The findings credit the gains. The report warns that the retirement savings of millions needed sharper guarding. The watch had to stay sharp.
openalex-w7207527522: Getting the right medicine to the right patient is a system, not a single act: selection, purchasing, storage, distribution, and counseling all matter. openalex-w7204548822: Twenty years after Brazil's universities adopted affirmative action, the State University of Bahia revised its own policy in August 2026. openalex-w7204479622: Hackers leave traces, but turning those traces into courtroom proof is hard. openalex-w7204156422: A cat with a sore in its mouth faced an aggressive cancer: oral squamous cell carcinoma. Clinical and concise, it documents a disease where speed matters.
openalex-w4396788322: Magnets tug on each other through quantum links, and the faint ones are hard to compute. openalex-w7204763522: Solid-state batteries need electrolytes that bake at lower heat. This paper tested special titanium- and germanium-based glasses as helpers for fusing LATP ceramic grains. arxiv-2606-16122: Many AI systems reason in words alone, but humans think with pictures too. arxiv-2606-16222: Large language models "think" in a compressed internal space before producing words. arxiv-2606-16622: Twist-lore sheets pen leapers in dales — dip zones of dash — and dales can hum as one. This paper charts dale-to-dale hum and tang-polar lean in three-dale twist packs. For twist-lore seers who read quirk phases in skewed sheets.
arxiv-2606-16722: Physicists who test tiny magnetic sensors need a room with almost no magnetic noise — and the same quiet every time. arxiv-2606-16822: Should AI just answer science questions, or help students DO science? This paper frames AI as a partner in learning about, doing, and engaging with science — with 'vigilance' (staying alert to AI errors) as the key to productive use. It is for science education researchers.
